projects.title: Insect colony
projects.description: Insect colony "HIVE" - Real-Time Resource Gathering Simulation (C# / .NET / WebSockets / Railway). Built from scratch using native C# WebSockets and a custom binary netcode protocol, replacing heavy JSON data streams to achieve ultra-low latency and minimal bandwidth (packets optimized down to 21-25 bytes). Features authoritarian server-side world generation with smart procedural resource clustering and real-time safe zone calculations. Fully containerized with Docker and deployed on cloud VPS infrastructure (Railway) supporting secure secure sockets (WSS) 24/7.

content.title: Source Code
content.content: Server GitHub Repository. A standalone, headless dedicated game server implemented as a lightweight C# .NET Core Console Application. It serves as the authoritative host for the game world, processing all state changes and player interactions. The architecture is engineered around the Fleck WebSocket library, driving a bespoke multi-threaded server loop that serializes and deserializes custom binary network streams. Instead of using standard game engine network wrappers, it implements direct byte-array manipulation to broadcast delta-compressed synchronization updates to connected clients in real time.

content.title: UCannotSurvive - beta
content.description: Fight for a righteous cause and rescue defenseless puppies from zombies—both the cunning ones and the not-so-cunning. Control your character using WASD, the arrow keys, or touch-like cursor inputs. Attacks are automated: targeting prioritizes zombies, meaning your character won't waste time breaking crates if enemies are nearby.

content.title: The codebase has undergone a major overhaul: all characters, including both the player and the zombies, now inherit from a single base script. Unique zombie types inherit from the base zombie class, overriding specific functions. Heavy methods like distance or setDestination run on a timer to minimize CPU overhead. The KISS principle was applied in several places—since the player's current weapon inventory is limited, it is hardcoded into the player script; as variety expands, weapons will be refactored into Scriptable Objects (SO). Damage dealing is handled via an interface. Additionally, all characters share a single material with custom UV mapping layouts. The Enemy Manager spawns all units with staggered delays to prevent frame drops.
